summary: This is a Mol Labs public report (P23) framing a research hypothesis ("assumption-kill") about whether exogenous oxytocin retains social-memory or anxiolytic phenotype under conditions where OXTR-class attribution is fully abolished (via OXTR antagonist or Oxtr genetic LOF). The document is a pre-registered discussion/proposal card, not a completed experiment, with execution status listed as NOT_RUN. It reviews prior literature (Ferguson, Takayanagi, Hung, Matsumoto, Tsai) that collectively argues AGAINST residual oxytocin activity under OXTR abolish, and identifies the matched residual H2H experiment as UNKNOWN.

content_blocks.title: Claim / Hypothesis (P23)
content_blocks.content: On a matched social-recognition / anxiolysis panel ± exogenous oxytocin ± OXTR antagonist or Oxtr genetic LOF (e.g. L-368,899, site-specific OXTR antagonist, or Oxtr-/- / cell-type Oxtr ablation) titrated so the block abolishes OXTR-class social-recognition / anxiolysis attribution, residual oxytocin social-memory / anxiolytic phenotype remains ≥50% of the oxytocin without-OXTR-abolish arm on the same panel. This is labeled an 'assumption-kill' / oxtr-insufficiency hypothesis. Status: NEGATIVE polarity; execution_status=NOT_RUN.

content_blocks.title: Scientific Rationale / Why It Matters
content_blocks.content: Ferguson maps OXTR activation in medial amygdala as necessary and sufficient for mouse social recognition. Takayanagi / Hung / Matsumoto map Oxtr LOF social-discrimination and allogrooming deficits. P23 asks whether residual exogenous oxytocin social-memory / anxiolysis under an OXTR antagonist or Oxtr LOF that abolishes OXTR-class attribution still requires a path beyond OXTR-class attribution (oxtr-insufficiency assumption-kill). The document explicitly distinguishes P23 from P15–P22 (different peptides/targets).

content_blocks.title: Mechanism Sketch
content_blocks.content: The oxtr-insufficiency assumption-kill is grounded in: (1) Ferguson OXTR MeA necessary and sufficient for social recognition (OT antagonist; OT peptide-KO rescue requires intact OXTR — necessity AGAINST residual); (2) Takayanagi Oxtr(-/-) social discrimination deficits; (3) Hung Oxtr mossy-cell social discrimination (cell-type necessity); (4) Matsumoto Oxtr indispensable allogrooming; (5) Promoted Tsai (PMID 35811321) showing PVH OXT-neuron SRM enhancement BLOCKED by L-368,899 into dCA2 — stronger necessity H2H AGAINST residual. None of these score residual exogenous oxytocin under an OXTR antagonist / Oxtr LOF that abolishes OXTR-class attribution on the same panel.

content_blocks.title: Baseline Measured / Evidence Status
content_blocks.content: Ferguson OXTR MeA necessary and sufficient: LITERATURE (PMID 11588199; necessity AGAINST residual). Takayanagi Oxtr(-/-) social discrimination: LITERATURE (PMID 16249339; phenotype without exogenous-OT residual arm). Hung Oxtr mossy-cell social discrimination: LITERATURE (PMID 37769745; cell-type necessity ≠ residual H2H). Matsumoto Oxtr indispensable allogrooming: LITERATURE (PMID 34057769; necessity ≠ residual H2H). Tsai PVH OXT-neuron SRM enhance BLOCKED by L-368,899 into dCA2: LITERATURE (PMID 35811321; necessity H2H AGAINST residual). Matched residual-positive exogenous oxytocin social-memory / anxiolysis under OXTR antagonist / Oxtr LOF: UNKNOWN. Residual ≥50% of oxytocin without-OXTR-abolish arm: PREDICTION (not yet observed).

content_blocks.title: Proposed Assay / Method
content_blocks.content: Method type: propose-assay. Preferred approach: MeA / mossy-cell / dCA2 circuit or slice block-QC with OXTR antagonist / Oxtr ablation before new animal social-recognition / anxiolysis panels. Key design elements: (1) Lock one social-recognition / anxiolysis panel; (2) ± exogenous oxytocin; (3) ± OXTR antagonist or Oxtr genetic LOF (e.g. L-368,899, site-specific OXTR antagonist, or Oxtr-/- / cell-type Oxtr ablation); (4) Block QC must abolish OXTR-class social-recognition / anxiolysis attribution; (5) Social-memory / anxiolytic readout; (6) ≥50%-of-oxytocin-without-OXTR-abolish residual gate. Refute condition: residual <50% of oxytocin without-OXTR-abolish arm when incomplete block and QC artifacts are ruled out.

content_blocks.title: Actionable Limitations
content_blocks.content: 1. Do not treat P1–P22 as proving P23 — Ferguson/Takayanagi/Hung/Matsumoto necessity priors are not a residual-under-OXTR-abolish H2H; Tsai L-368899 block leans AGAINST residual; soft-complete empty ≠ demonstrated residual phenotype; do not invent residual when UNKNOWN. 2. Skip-list / series distinctness — do not freeze or collapse to OpenLabs BPC orthosteric dialect, P15–P22 series, or FOXO4×LOF (SERIES_FROZEN). 3. Ferguson/Takayanagi/Hung/Matsumoto lack an exogenous-OT residual arm under OXTR-abolish on the same panel; incomplete OXTR block / OXTR-class attribution not abolished / no residual to score / block-QC failure leave the test inconclusive rather than refuted.

key_findings: P23 is a pre-registered hypothesis (NOT_RUN) asking whether exogenous oxytocin retains ≥50% social-memory or anxiolytic phenotype under OXTR antagonist or Oxtr genetic LOF that abolishes OXTR-class attribution — the matched residual H2H result is UNKNOWN.

All four key prior-art studies (Ferguson PMID 11588199, Takayanagi PMID 16249339, Hung PMID 37769745, Matsumoto PMID 34057769) provide necessity evidence AGAINST residual oxytocin activity under OXTR abolish, but none include an exogenous-OT residual arm under OXTR-abolish on the same panel.

Promoted Tsai (PMID 35811321) shows PVH OXT-neuron social recognition memory enhancement is BLOCKED by L-368,899 into dCA2 — the strongest H2H evidence AGAINST residual, but still not a matched residual-positive result.
The ≥50% residual threshold is an author-chosen PREDICTION, not an observed effect; no dosing data, no quantitative experimental results are present in this document.
Execution status is NOT_RUN; FTO status is UNKNOWN; the document is a research-discussion proposal card with negative polarity and kill_cost_tier=1 (estimated 4 weeks to refute).

The document explicitly distinguishes P23 from P15–P22 (BPC/FBXO22, LKKTETQ, MOTS-c, SS-31, ARA290, Semax, Selank, Dihexa) and from FOXO4×LOF (SERIES_FROZEN), emphasizing that none of those prior series constitute proof for P23.
Proposed assay prefers MeA / mossy-cell / dCA2 circuit or slice block-QC with OXTR antagonist / Oxtr ablation before new animal social-recognition / anxiolysis panels.
